reasons.C: Closest in movement: long, semicolon-joined sentences broken by short assertive ones, dry irony and firm assertion without hedging, period spelling ('any one', 'To-day'), and long dense paragraphs like the passage's.
reasons.A: Good period cadence and semicolon habit with plain assertions ('This is not a lament.'), but the parenthetical exclamation and the 'I fancy' and 'I grant' asides lean more whimsical and confiding than the passage's colder, argumentative tone.
reasons.D: Right register, but it piles on the mannerisms: exclamations, parenthetical asides, many dashes and coy 'I have been given to understand' phrasing, all in short paragraphs. It reads as imitation more than as the author.
reasons.B: Modern plain-essay voice: short, evenly weighted sentences, no semicolons, contemporary diction ('holds the keys', 'who is winning') and many short paragraphs. Nothing of the passage's period rhythm or ironic assertion.
